mcp.title: Use TimeIQ inside Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor
mcp.description: Check your availability, find group meeting times, import schedules, log hours and prepare invoices from your AI assistant. Connect TimeIQ with MCP.
mcp.ogAlt: TimeIQ: all your calendars, one booking link
mcp.heading: Use TimeIQ inside Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor.
mcp.lead: Your calendars, meetings, hours and invoices, connected to your AI assistant through MCP. Ask when you’re free, log client work or prepare an invoice in the chat you already have open.
mcp.worksWith: Works with your connected calendars and TimeIQ account.
mcp.setupLead: Choose your client. Use the hosted server URL below, then connect your TimeIQ account.

claude.title: Claude on the web or desktop
claude.step1: Open Settings → Connectors (called Customize → Connectors in some versions).
claude.step2: Choose Add custom connector and name it TimeIQ.
claude.step4: Connect, sign in to TimeIQ and select Allow. Enable TimeIQ in the chat’s connectors menu.
claude.note: On a managed workspace, an owner may need to add the connector first. <link>Claude’s connector guide</link>

chatgpt.step1: Open Settings → Connectors (or Apps), then enable developer mode under advanced settings if needed.
chatgpt.step2: Add a custom connector or app named TimeIQ.
chatgpt.step3: Set its MCP server URL to {url}.
chatgpt.step4: Connect, sign in to TimeIQ and select Allow. Select TimeIQ in your conversation’s tools menu.
chatgpt.note: Custom connectors depend on your ChatGPT plan and workspace permissions. If the option is missing, check with your workspace owner. <link>OpenAI’s connection guide</link>

code.intro: Run this in a terminal. Complete the browser sign-in when prompted and select Allow. If needed, run /mcp in Claude Code to authenticate TimeIQ.
code.token: You can also connect with a personal token. In TimeIQ, open <link>Settings → AI assistants</link>, create a token, then replace the placeholder below with it.

cursor.title: Cursor and other MCP clients
cursor.intro: Create a personal token in Settings → AI assistants. In Cursor, add this to your MCP configuration (~/.cursor/mcp.json), replacing YOUR_TIMEIQ_TOKEN with the token.
cursor.others: For other clients, use the same URL and Authorization header with Streamable HTTP. Keep your token private and outside shared project files. <link>Cursor’s MCP guide</link>

mcp.selfHost: Self-hosting? Your endpoint is {endpoint}. Replace the hosted server URL in these instructions with yours.

mcp.safety1: Tools that email people or change shared calendars ask you first. TimeIQ instructs your assistant to confirm and marks these tools for client approval. Keep approvals enabled in your client.
mcp.safety2: Manage connections and revoke personal tokens in <link>Settings → AI assistants</link>. A revoked token stops working immediately.
mcp.safety3: Tokens cannot delete your account or create other tokens. TimeIQ is open source: <link>read the code on GitHub</link>.

what.a: The Model Context Protocol is a standard for connecting an AI assistant to an app’s tools. TimeIQ’s MCP server lets your assistant work with your TimeIQ account from a conversation.

account.q: Do I need a TimeIQ account?
account.a: Yes. Sign up, connect your calendars and set your working hours in TimeIQ. Your assistant uses that same account. The hosted service follows your TimeIQ subscription; your assistant may have its own plan or workspace requirements for custom connectors.

privacy.q: Can it see other people’s calendars?
privacy.a: It reads calendars connected to your account. For a group meeting, it suggests times you are free and asks participants to share their availability through a link. It does not gain access to their private calendars.

fails.a: Check that the server URL ends in /mcp and that you have signed in and allowed the connection. For token setup, send Authorization: Bearer followed by your full token. If you revoked or lost it, create a new token in Settings → AI assistants. Check that your TimeIQ subscription is active and your client allows custom connectors.

selfHost.q: Can I use a different client or self-host TimeIQ?
selfHost.a: Yes. Use an MCP client that supports Streamable HTTP and either browser sign-in or an Authorization header. For a self-hosted installation, replace the hosted URL with your own API’s /mcp endpoint. Cloud clients need to be able to reach that URL.
